name: Session player: pixel-perfect replay in the browser
summary: The HQ scrubber replays the recorded event stream honestly, but it draws markers, not the game. This project is the real thing: the game's own renderer playing a session's replay in the browser, via a Godot web export of a dedicated session-player scene. The attract loop already proved the renderer runs standalone off a replay with a detached state; this adds step/seek controls bridged to the page (Godot web exports support JS interop), a session picker fed by HQ, and time-compressed playback.
requirements: A session-player scene: loads any playtests/<name>/session_replay.json, drives a detached world exactly as the attract loop does
Step forward/back by action, seek to any action index, play at compressed pacing — controlled from the HQ page via the JS bridge

Honest versioning: the player shows the session's build stamp and warns when it differs from the running build (an old replay on new worldgen renders a reconstruction, not the original — say so on screen)
Web export of just this scene served by the HQ server; no effect on the game's own exports
The HQ scrubber remains the fallback for sessions whose replays no longer reproduce
current_status: Planned. The technical spine exists (attract loop, replay format, web export pipeline); the new work is the control bridge, the export packaging, and the build-mismatch honesty layer.

plan.step: HQ event scrubber shipped (the honest marker-level playback)
Session-player scene over the attract-loop machinery, with step/seek
JS bridge + HQ embedding with session picker
Build-stamp honesty: reconstruction warnings for cross-build replays
